results.title: Frobenius and spectral norms: mixed inequalities
results.informal: Submultiplicativity: $\|AB\|_F \le \|A\|\,\|B\|_F$ and $\|AB\|_F \le \|A\|_F\,\|B\|$. Norm comparison: $\|A\| \le \|A\|_F \le \sqrt{\operatorname{rank}(A)}\,\|A\|$. Both norms are unitarily invariant, and $$\|A\|_F^2 = \operatorname{tr}(A^\top A) = \sum_i \sigma_i^2.$$

results.title: Singular value decomposition of a matrix
results.informal: Every $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ factors as $A = U\Sigma V^\top$ with $U, V$ orthogonal and $\Sigma$ diagonal with $\sigma_1 \ge \dots \ge \sigma_{\min(m,n)} \ge 0$. Splitting at rank $k$ gives the block form $$A = U_1\Sigma_1V_1^\top + U_2\Sigma_2V_2^\top.$$
results.conclusion: $A = U\Sigma V^\top$ with $U, V$ orthogonal and $\Sigma$ diagonal with $\sigma_1 \ge \dots \ge \sigma_{\min(m,n)} \ge 0$; at rank $k$, $A = U_1\Sigma_1V_1^\top + U_2\Sigma_2V_2^\top$

formalizations.note: IsSVD A U V: Uᵀ U = 1, Vᵀ V = 1, A = U · rectDiag (singularValues A) · Vᵀ, where singularValues A : ℕ → ℝ is Mathlib's LinearMap.singularValues of toEuclideanLin A (zero-indexed, antitone, zero beyond the rank). Also uniqueness of σ, block split at k (IsSVD.eq_head_add_tail), AᵀA and AAᵀ diagonalisations, frobSq = Σσ², invariance under orthogonal factors and transpose.

results.title: Eckart–Young–Mirsky: best rank-k approximation
results.informal: Both minima are attained by the truncated SVD $\lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k$: $$\min_{\operatorname{rank} B \le k} \|A - B\| = \sigma_{k+1}(A), \qquad \min_{\operatorname{rank} B \le k} \|A - B\|_F^2 = \sum_{i>k} \sigma_i^2.$$
results.conclusion: $\min_{\operatorname{rank} B \le k} \|A - B\| = \sigma_{k+1}(A)$ and $\min_{\operatorname{rank} B \le k} \|A - B\|_F^2 = \sum_{i>k} \sigma_i^2$, both attained by $\lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k$
results.notes: OPT in every low-rank bound. The LRA project currently takes 'IsBestRankApprox' as a hypothesis (rank_mul_le_of_isBestRankApprox).

results.title: Weyl and Mirsky perturbation bounds for singular values
results.informal: For every $i$, $|\sigma_i(A+E) - \sigma_i(A)| \le \|E\|$, and $$\Big(\sum_i \big(\sigma_i(A+E) - \sigma_i(A)\big)^2\Big)^{1/2} \le \|E\|_F.$$

results.title: Courant–Fischer min-max and Rayleigh quotients
results.informal: For Hermitian $A$, $$\lambda_k(A) = \max_{\dim S = k}\ \min_{x \in S,\ \|x\|=1} x^\top A x.$$ In particular $\lambda_{\max}$ is the sup of the Rayleigh quotient and $\lambda_{\min}$ the inf.
results.conclusion: $\lambda_k(A) = \max_{\dim S = k}\ \min_{x \in S,\ \|x\|=1} x^\top A x$; in particular $\lambda_{\max} = \sup_{\|x\|=1} x^\top Ax$ and $\lambda_{\min} = \inf_{\|x\|=1} x^\top Ax$

results.notes: The user's definitions lambdaMax/lambdaMin (Tropp) and lamMin (LRA) are both the Rayleigh form; the full min-max is what interlacing and Weyl need.

results.title: Cauchy interlacing for principal submatrices and compressions
results.informal: If $Q$ has $k$ orthonormal columns then $$\lambda_{i+n-k}(A) \le \lambda_i(Q^\top A Q) \le \lambda_i(A).$$ Used for Nyström, Lanczos/Ritz values and column subset selection.

results.title: Rank: products, sums, and rank-k matrices
results.informal: $\operatorname{rank}(AB) \le \min(\operatorname{rank} A, \operatorname{rank} B)$; $\operatorname{rank}(A+B) \le \operatorname{rank} A + \operatorname{rank} B$; $\operatorname{rank}(QX) = \operatorname{rank} X$ for $Q$ with orthonormal columns.
results.conclusion: $\operatorname{rank}(AB) \le \min(\operatorname{rank} A, \operatorname{rank} B)$, $\operatorname{rank}(A+B) \le \operatorname{rank} A + \operatorname{rank} B$ and $\operatorname{rank}(QX) = \operatorname{rank} X$

results.title: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse and its identities
results.informal: $A^\dagger$ is defined via the SVD and satisfies the four Penrose identities. $A^\dagger = (A^\top A)^{-1}A^\top$ for full column rank and $A^\top(AA^\top)^{-1}$ for full row rank. $AA^\dagger$ is the orthogonal projector onto $\operatorname{range}(A)$; $\|A^\dagger\| = 1/\sigma_{\min}$; and $\|G^\dagger\|_F^2 = \operatorname{tr}\big((GG^\top)^{-1}\big)$.
hypotheses: the pseudoinverse $A^\dagger \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$ (Lean: $\operatorname{pinvL} A = (A^\top A)^{-1}A^\top$, $\operatorname{pinvR} A = A^\top(AA^\top)^{-1}$)
results.conclusion: $A^\dagger = (A^\top A)^{-1}A^\top$ for full column rank and $A^\top(AA^\top)^{-1}$ for full row rank, satisfying $AA^\dagger A = A$, $A^\dagger AA^\dagger = A^\dagger$, $(AA^\dagger)^\top = AA^\dagger$, $(A^\dagger A)^\top = A^\dagger A$; moreover $\|A^\dagger\| = 1/\sigma_{\min}$ and $\|G^\dagger\|_F^2 = \operatorname{tr}\big((GG^\top)^{-1}\big)$

results.title: Orthogonal projectors and residuals
results.informal: For $Q$ with orthonormal columns, $P = QQ^\top$ is an orthogonal projector and $\|A\|_F^2 = \|PA\|_F^2 + \|(I-P)A\|_F^2$. If $\operatorname{range}(A\Omega) \subseteq \operatorname{range}(Q)$ then $(I-P)A\Omega = 0$. Projection error is monotone under range inclusion.

results.title: Completing an orthonormal frame to an orthogonal matrix
results.informal: If $Q \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times q}$ has orthonormal columns, there is $Q_\perp \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times(m-q)}$ with $[Q\ \ Q_\perp]$ orthogonal: $$QQ^\top + Q_\perp Q_\perp^\top = I, \qquad Q^\top Q_\perp = 0.$$

results.title: Loewner order and the continuous functional calculus on matrices
results.informal: $A \preceq B$ iff $B - A$ is PSD. Trace and conjugation are monotone. $f(A)$ for Hermitian $A$ is defined via the eigendecomposition, including $\sqrt{A}$, $\exp A$ and $\log A$.
results.conclusion: $A \preceq B \iff B - A \succeq 0$, and $f(A) = \sum_i f(\lambda_i)\,u_iu_i^*$ (including $\sqrt{A}$, $\exp A$, $\log A$); trace and conjugation are monotone

results.title: Isserlis / Wick formula for Gaussian moments
results.informal: $\mathbb{E}[g_{i_1}\cdots g_{i_{2k}}]$ is the sum over pairings of products of covariances. General engine for all polynomial moments (fourth moments, Hutchinson variance, AMM).
hypotheses: $g = (g_1, \dots, g_n)$ a centred Gaussian vector with covariance $C$
results.conclusion: $\mathbb{E}[g_{i_1}\cdots g_{i_{2k}}] = \sum_{\pi} \prod_{\{a,b\} \in \pi} C_{i_a i_b}$, the sum over all pairings $\pi$ of $\{1, \dots, 2k\}$
results.notes: Special cases (fourth moments) are proved by hand; the general formula would remove the case-by-case work.

results.title: Norm of a matrix with independent sub-Gaussian rows
aliases: extreme singular values of sub-Gaussian matrices
results.informal: For $A \in \mathbb{R}^{N\times n}$ with isotropic sub-Gaussian rows, with probability at least $1 - 2e^{-ct^2}$, $$\sqrt{N} - C\sqrt{n} - t \le \sigma_{\min}(A) \le \sigma_{\max}(A) \le \sqrt{N} + C\sqrt{n} + t.$$ Gives subspace embeddings for Rademacher and other dense sketches.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb{R}^{N\times n}$ with independent isotropic sub-Gaussian rows
$t \ge 0$; constants $c, C$ depending only on the sub-Gaussian norm
results.conclusion: with probability at least $1 - 2e^{-ct^2}$, $\sqrt{N} - C\sqrt{n} - t \le \sigma_{\min}(A) \le \sigma_{\max}(A) \le \sqrt{N} + C\sqrt{n} + t$

results.title: Markov and Chebyshev inequalities
results.informal: $\mathbb{P}[X \ge t] \le \mathbb{E}X/t$ and $\mathbb{P}\big[|X - \mathbb{E}X| \ge t\big] \le \operatorname{Var}X/t^2$.

results.title: Chernoff bound for sums of independent sub-Gaussian variables
aliases: tail of sums of sub-Gaussian variables
results.informal: For independent $X_i$ with sub-Gaussian MGFs: $$\mathbb{P}\Big[\sum_i X_i \ge t\Big] \le \exp\Big(-\frac{t^2}{2\sum_i c_i}\Big).$$
hypotheses: $X_i$ has a sub-Gaussian MGF with parameter $c_i$

results.title: Hoeffding's lemma and inequality
results.informal: Bounded $X \in [a,b]$ is sub-Gaussian with $c = (b-a)^2/4$; this gives the tail for bounded independent sums.
hypotheses: $X_1, \dots, X_N$ independent with $X_i \in [a_i, b_i]$ almost surely

formalizations.note: Hoeffding's lemma in MGF form

results.title: Bernstein inequality (sub-exponential sums)
results.informal: Tail for sums of centered sub-exponential variables, with the variance/range crossover.
hypotheses: $X_1, \dots, X_N$ independent, centred, sub-exponential with $\|X_i\|_{\psi_1} \le K$

results.title: Hanson–Wright inequality
results.informal: For $x$ with independent sub-Gaussian coordinates: $$\mathbb{P}\big[|x^\top Ax - \mathbb{E}x^\top Ax| \ge t\big] \le 2\exp\Big(-c\min\Big(\frac{t^2}{K^4\|A\|_F^2}, \frac{t}{K^2\|A\|}\Big)\Big).$$ The tail bound behind trace estimation and JL for sub-Gaussian sketches.

formalizations.note: constant hansonWrightUniversalConstant = 1/(4·64·e²); hypotheses iIndepFun X μ and ∀ i, HasSubgaussianMGF (X i) K² μ; conclusion on |centeredQuadraticForm| with its own Frobenius/operator norm definitions. Port, do not depend (Lean v4.29.1 pin).

results.title: McDiarmid's bounded-differences inequality
results.informal: Concentration of functions with bounded coordinate-wise differences. Used for sampling-based sketches.
hypotheses: $|f(x) - f(x')| \le c_i$ whenever $x, x'$ differ only in coordinate $i$

results.title: Matrix Laplace transform method and master bounds
aliases: subadditivity of matrix cumulant generating functions
results.informal: For independent Hermitian summands $X_k$ with $Y = \sum_k X_k$: $$\mathbb{E}\,\lambda_{\max}(Y) \le \inf_{\theta>0} \frac{1}{\theta}\log\operatorname{tr}\exp\Big(\sum_k \log\mathbb{E}\,e^{\theta X_k}\Big),$$ and the matching tail bound.
hypotheses: $X_1, \dots, X_N$ independent random Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices
results.conclusion: $\mathbb{E}\,\lambda_{\max}(Y) \le \inf_{\theta>0} \frac{1}{\theta}\log\operatorname{tr}\exp\Big(\sum_k \log\mathbb{E}\,e^{\theta X_k}\Big)$ and $\mathbb{P}[\lambda_{\max}(Y) \ge t] \le \inf_{\theta>0} e^{-\theta t}\operatorname{tr}\exp\Big(\sum_k \log\mathbb{E}\,e^{\theta X_k}\Big)$

formalizations.usage: Pass independent (`hIndep : iIndepFun X μ`), measurable, a.e.-Hermitian, integrable `X : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ` and `hExp` (integrability of `matrixExp (θ • X k)`); for `0 < θ` gives the `lambdaMax` expectation and tail bounds in terms of `traceExp (cumulantSum μ X θ)`, and for `θ < 0` the `lambdaMin` analogues.

results.title: Matrix Gaussian and Rademacher series
results.informal: $$\mathbb{E}\Big\|\sum_k \gamma_k A_k\Big\| \le \sqrt{2\sigma^2\log(d_1+d_2)}$$ with $\sigma^2 = \max\big(\|\sum_k A_kA_k^\top\|, \|\sum_k A_k^\top A_k\|\big)$.
hypotheses: $\gamma_k$ independent, all standard Gaussian or all Rademacher
results.conclusion: $\mathbb{E}\Big\|\sum_k \gamma_k A_k\Big\| \le \sqrt{2\sigma^2\log(d_1+d_2)}$, with the matching tail bound

formalizations.usage: Pass fixed `B : Fin N → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℂ` and independent measurable scalars `g` with `hLaw` (all standard Gaussian or all Rademacher); for `Z = ∑ g k • B k` with second moment `v`, gives `v = max ‖∑ B Bᴴ‖ ‖∑ Bᴴ B‖`, `E spectralNorm Z ≤ √(2 v log(m + n))` and the tail `gaussianSeriesTail (m + n) v t`.

results.title: Matrix Chernoff inequality
results.informal: Upper and lower tails for $\lambda_{\max}$ and $\lambda_{\min}$ of a sum of independent PSD matrices bounded by $L$.
hypotheses: $X_1, \dots, X_N$ independent random PSD $d\times d$ matrices
results.conclusion: $\mathbb{P}[\lambda_{\min}(Y) \le (1-\varepsilon)\mu_{\min}] \le d\Big[\frac{e^{-\varepsilon}}{(1-\varepsilon)^{1-\varepsilon}}\Big]^{\mu_{\min}/L}$ for $0 \le \varepsilon < 1$ and $\mathbb{P}[\lambda_{\max}(Y) \ge (1+\varepsilon)\mu_{\max}] \le d\Big[\frac{e^{\varepsilon}}{(1+\varepsilon)^{1+\varepsilon}}\Big]^{\mu_{\max}/L}$ for $\varepsilon \ge 0$, with matching expectation bounds

formalizations.usage: Pass independent, measurable, a.e.-Hermitian `X k` with `hBound : 0 ≤ lambdaMin (X k) ∧ lambdaMax (X k) ≤ L` a.e. and `hL : 0 ≤ L`; with `a`, `b` the extreme eigenvalues of `E ∑ X k`, gives expectation bounds for every `θ > 0`, the lower tail `chernoffLowerTail d a L ε` (`0 ≤ ε < 1`) and the upper tail `chernoffUpperTail d b L ε` (`0 ≤ ε`).

results.title: Matrix Bernstein inequality
results.informal: Tail and expectation bounds for $\|\sum_k S_k\|$ with $\|S_k\| \le L$ and matrix variance $v$.

formalizations.usage: Pass independent, measurable, centred (`hMean`) `S k : Ω → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℂ` with `hBound : spectralNorm (S k) ≤ L` a.e. and `0 ≤ L`; for `Z = ∑ S k` and `v = rectSecondMoment μ Z` gives the formula for `v`, `E spectralNorm Z ≤ √(2 v log(m + n)) + L log(m + n) / 3` and the tail `bernsteinTail (m + n) v L t`.

Pass independent, centred, a.e.-Hermitian `X k` with `hL2 : MemLp (X k) 2 μ` and `hBound : lambdaMax (X k) ≤ L` a.e.; gives `v = spectralNorm (∑ E X k ^ 2)`, `E lambdaMax (∑ X k) ≤ √(2 v log d) + L log d / 3` and the tail `bernsteinTail d v L t`.

results.title: Intrinsic-dimension Chernoff and Bernstein
results.informal: Replaces $\log d$ with $\log\operatorname{intdim}(V)$.
hypotheses: independent random matrices as in matrix Chernoff or Bernstein
a semidefinite upper bound $V$ on $\mathbb{E}Y$ (Chernoff) or on the matrix variance (Bernstein)
results.conclusion: the matrix Chernoff and Bernstein bounds hold with the ambient dimension replaced by $\operatorname{intdim}(V)$, e.g. $\mathbb{P}[\|Z\| \ge t] \le 4\operatorname{intdim}(V)\exp\Big(\frac{-t^2/2}{v + Lt/3}\Big)$ for $t \ge \sqrt{v} + L/3$

formalizations.usage: Pass independent PSD `X k` with `lambdaMax (X k) ≤ L` a.e. (`0 < L`) and a nonzero `M` with `hMeanBound : loewnerLE (E ∑ X k) M`; with `r = intrinsicDimension M`, `a = lambdaMax M`, gives `E lambdaMax ≤ (e^θ − 1)/θ · a + (L/θ) log(2r)` for `θ > 0` and the tail `2 r exp((a/L)(ε − (1+ε) log(1+ε)))` for `ε ≥ L/a`.

Pass independent centred `S k` with `spectralNorm (S k) ≤ L` a.e. and variance proxies `V₁`, `V₂` (not both 0) with `loewnerLE (E Z Zᴴ) V₁` and `loewnerLE (E Zᴴ Z) V₂`; with `r = intrinsicDimension (fromBlocks V₁ 0 0 V₂)` and `v = max ‖V₁‖ ‖V₂‖`, gives `P[t ≤ spectralNorm Z] ≤ 4 r exp(−(t²/2)/(v + L t/3))` for `t ≥ √v + L/3`.

results.title: Sampling lemma: sums of independent rank-one PSD samples
results.informal: If the $x_j$ are i.i.d. with $\mathbb{E}\,x_jx_j^\top = I$ and $\|x_j\|^2 \le L$ a.s., then $\frac{1}{k}\sum_j x_jx_j^\top$ has eigenvalues in $[1-\varepsilon, 1+\varepsilon]$ with probability at least $1 - 2d\exp(-k\varepsilon^2/(cL))$. The one corollary of matrix Chernoff that every sampling-based embedding uses.
results.conclusion: with probability at least $1 - 2d\exp(-k\varepsilon^2/(cL))$, every eigenvalue of $\frac{1}{k}\sum_j x_jx_j^\top$ lies in $[1-\varepsilon, 1+\varepsilon]$
results.notes: Matrix Chernoff is proved; this packaging is cheap and unlocks SRHT, leverage-score sampling and sparsification.

results.title: Matrix Freedman / martingale Bernstein
results.informal: Martingale version of matrix Bernstein; used for adaptive sampling and streaming.

results.title: Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma
results.informal: $n$ points embed into $k = O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log n)$ dimensions with all pairwise distances preserved to within $1 \pm \varepsilon$; union bound over the distributional lemma.
results.conclusion: there is a linear $S : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^k$ with $(1-\varepsilon)\|p_i - p_j\|^2 \le \|S(p_i - p_j)\|^2 \le (1+\varepsilon)\|p_i - p_j\|^2$ for all $i, j$; the Gaussian sketch $k^{-1/2}G$ works with probability at least $1/2$

formalizations.usage: For points `p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ` and `0 < ε < 1`; bounds the `gaussianMatrix k n`-measure of sketches distorting some pair `i ≠ j` by more than `1 ± ε` by `ENNReal.ofReal (N² · 2 exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6)))` (rests on the `jl_distributional` scaffold).

Pass `0 < ε < 1`, `hN : 2 ≤ N` and `hk : 48 * log N / ε² ≤ k`; gives that the bad set of Gaussian sketches has measure at most `ENNReal.ofReal (1/2)`.
Pass `0 < ε < 1`, `hN : 2 ≤ N` and `hk : 48 * log N / ε² ≤ k`; gives `∃ S` with `(1 − ε)‖p i − p j‖² ≤ ‖S (p i − p j)‖² ≤ (1 + ε)‖p i − p j‖²` for all `i j` (inherits the `jl_distributional` sorry).

results.informal: Same conclusion for Rademacher and other sub-Gaussian entries, from Hanson–Wright.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb{R}^{k\times n}$ with independent, centred, unit-variance sub-Gaussian entries and $S = k^{-1/2}A$

results.title: Subspace embedding: definition and equivalent forms
results.informal: $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{range}(U)$ ($U$ orthonormal) iff $\|SUx\|^2 \in (1\pm\varepsilon)\|x\|^2$ for all $x$, iff $\sigma(SU) \subset [\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}, \sqrt{1+\varepsilon}]$, iff $\|U^\top S^\top SU - I\| \le \varepsilon$. Oblivious vs. data-dependent variants.
results.conclusion: $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{range}(U)$ iff $(1-\varepsilon)\|x\|^2 \le \|SUx\|^2 \le (1+\varepsilon)\|x\|^2$ for all $x$, iff $\sigma(SU) \subset [\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}, \sqrt{1+\varepsilon}]$, iff $\|U^\top S^\top SU - I\| \le \varepsilon$

formalizations.note: definition, orthonormal-basis form, basis independence, monotonicity, and the Gram-form sufficient condition ‖(SU)ᵀSU − I‖ ≤ ε. Open: converse of the Gram form and the singular-value form (needs svd).
formalizations.usage: `IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε : Prop` says `S` is an ε-subspace embedding for `range U`; work with it through `isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_of_orthonormal` (needs `Uᵀ * U = 1`) or prove it from the Gram form `isSubspaceEmbedding_of_specNorm_gram_sub_one_le`.
Pass `hU : Uᵀ * U = 1`; rewrites `IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε` as `∀ x, (1 − ε) * x ⬝ᵥ x ≤ ‖(S * U) x‖² ∧ ‖(S * U) x‖² ≤ (1 + ε) * x ⬝ᵥ x` (squared norms written with `mulVec` and `⬝ᵥ`).
Pass `hC : IsUnit C.det`; rewrites `IsSubspaceEmbedding S (U * C) ε ↔ IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε` (only the subspace matters).
Pass `hU : Uᵀ * U = 1` and `h : specNorm ((S * U)ᵀ * (S * U) - 1) ≤ ε`; gives `IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε`.
From `h : IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε` and `hεε' : ε ≤ ε'`; gives `IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε'`.

results.notes: The vocabulary of modern RandNLA; every sketch result is stated against it.

results.title: Gaussian matrices are oblivious subspace embeddings
results.informal: $k^{-1/2}G$ with $k \ge C(d + \log(1/\delta))/\varepsilon^2$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for any fixed $d$-dimensional subspace with probability $1 - \delta$.
results.conclusion: with probability at least $1 - \delta$, $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{range}(U)$
results.notes: One line from the Mission III goal plus rotation invariance.

results.title: Subsampled randomized Hadamard transform is a subspace embedding
results.informal: SRHT with $k = O\big(\varepsilon^{-2}(d + \log n)\log d\big)$ rows is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding. Proof: row flattening by random signs, then matrix Chernoff sampling.
hypotheses: $S = \sqrt{n/k}\,RHD$ with $D$ random signs, $H$ the normalized Walsh–Hadamard matrix, $R$ sampling $k$ rows
results.conclusion: with high probability, $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{range}(U)$

formalizations.note: a rerandomized variant with prescribed width k = O(r/ε²); not the classical statement

results.title: Sparse oblivious subspace embeddings (CountSketch, OSNAP, SparseStack)
results.informal: CountSketch with $k = O(d^2/\varepsilon^2)$ rows is an OSE; OSNAP/SparseStack with $O(d/\varepsilon^2)$ rows and few nonzeros per column.
hypotheses: $S \in \mathbb{R}^{k\times n}$ a CountSketch (one random $\pm 1$ per column) or OSNAP/SparseStack (a few nonzeros per column)
$k = O(d^2/\varepsilon^2)$ for CountSketch, $k = O(d/\varepsilon^2)$ (up to log factors) for OSNAP/SparseStack
results.conclusion: with constant probability, $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{range}(U)$

results.title: Approximate matrix multiplication by row sampling
results.informal: Sampling $c$ column/row pairs with probabilities $p_i \propto \|A_{:,i}\|\,\|B_{i,:}\|$ gives $$\mathbb{E}\|AB - CR\|_F^2 \le \frac{\|A\|_F^2\|B\|_F^2}{c}.$$
hypotheses: $C$, $R$ the sampled columns of $A$ and rows of $B$, rescaled by $1/\sqrt{c\,p_i}$

results.title: Approximate multiplication from a subspace embedding
results.informal: If $S$ satisfies the JL moment property then $$\mathbb{E}\|A^\top S^\top SB - A^\top B\|_F^2 \le \varepsilon^2\|A\|_F^2\|B\|_F^2.$$ The glue between embeddings and least squares.
hypotheses: $S$ satisfies the JL moment property with parameter $\varepsilon$

results.title: Leverage scores: definition and basic properties
aliases: row norms of an orthonormal basis
results.informal: $\ell_i(A) = \|U_{i,:}\|^2 = (AA^\dagger)_{ii}$; $\sum_i \ell_i = \operatorname{rank} A$; $0 \le \ell_i \le 1$; invariant under change of basis of $\operatorname{range}(A)$.
results.conclusion: $\ell_i(A) = \|U_{i,:}\|^2 = (AA^\dagger)_{ii}$, with $\sum_i \ell_i = \operatorname{rank} A$, $0 \le \ell_i \le 1$, independent of the choice of $U$

results.title: Leverage-score row sampling is a subspace embedding
results.informal: Sampling $k = O(\varepsilon^{-2}d\log(d/\delta))$ rows with $p_i \propto \ell_i$ and rescaling gives an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding with probability $1 - \delta$. The same theorem gives spectral sparsification.
hypotheses: $k = O(\varepsilon^{-2}d\log(d/\delta))$ rows sampled i.i.d. with $p_i \propto \ell_i$ and rescaled by $1/\sqrt{kp_i}$
results.conclusion: with probability at least $1 - \delta$, the sampling matrix $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{range}(A)$

results.title: Volume sampling and column subset selection
results.informal: Sampling $k$ columns with probability proportional to squared volume gives $$\mathbb{E}\|A - \pi_S(A)\|_F^2 \le (k+1)\,\|A - \lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k\|_F^2.$$
hypotheses: a set $S$ of $k$ columns sampled with probability proportional to $\det(A_S^\top A_S)$
$\pi_S$ the orthogonal projection onto the span of the chosen columns

results.title: Deterministic range-finder bound, Frobenius form
aliases: deterministic error bound for randomized range finding
results.informal: If $\operatorname{range}(A\Omega) \subseteq \operatorname{range}(Q)$ and $\Omega_1 = V_1^\top\Omega$ has full row rank, then $$\|(I-QQ^\top)A\|_F^2 \le \|\Sigma_2\|_F^2 + \|\Sigma_2\Omega_2\Omega_1^\dagger\|_F^2.$$
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ with block SVD $A = U_1\Sigma_1V_1^\top + U_2\Sigma_2V_2^\top$

formalizations.note: HMT Thm 9.1, Frobenius form, slightly more general than the source (no diagonal S, no U₁ hypotheses); plus the truncated variant (Chen–Persson prop:hmt-struct)
formalizations.usage: Pass the block split `hA : A = U₁ * S₁ * V₁ᵀ + U₂ * S₂ * V₂ᵀ` with `U₂ᵀU₂ = 1`, `V₁ᵀV₁ = 1`, `V₂ᵀV₂ = 1`, `V₁ᵀV₂ = 0` (no diagonality, nothing on `U₁`), `hΩ₁ : Ω₁ = V₁ᵀ * Ω`, `hΩ₂ : Ω₂ = V₂ᵀ * Ω`, `hunit : IsUnit (Ω₁ * Ω₁ᵀ)`, `hQo : Qᵀ * Q = 1` and `hQ : Q * (Qᵀ * (A * Ω)) = A * Ω`; gives `frobSq (residual Q A) ≤ frobSq S₂ + frobSq (S₂ * Ω₂ * pinvR Ω₁)`.
Same hypotheses as `rangeFinder_frobSq_le` plus `hY : IsBestRankApprox k (Qᵀ * A) Y` (`k` = number of columns of `V₁`); gives `frobSq (A - Q * Y) ≤ frobSq S₂ + frobSq (S₂ * Ω₂ * pinvR Ω₁)`.

Pass the block-SVD hypotheses (`hA`, `hU₂`, `hV₁`, `hV₂`, `hV`), `hΩ₁`, `hΩ₂` and `hunit : IsUnit (Ω₁ * Ω₁ᵀ)` (no `Q`); gives the exact identity `frobSq (A - A * Ω * pinvR Ω₁ * V₁ᵀ) = frobSq S₂ + frobSq (S₂ * Ω₂ * pinvR Ω₁)`.

results.title: Deterministic range-finder bound, spectral form
aliases: deterministic range finder bound, spectral norm
results.informal: Under the same hypotheses: $$\|(I-QQ^\top)A\|^2 \le \|\Sigma_2\|^2 + \|\Sigma_2\Omega_2\Omega_1^\dagger\|^2.$$
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ with block SVD $A = U_1\Sigma_1V_1^\top + U_2\Sigma_2V_2^\top$
results.notes: The Frobenius form is proved; the spectral form needs ‖[X Y]‖² ≤ ‖X‖² + ‖Y‖² style block norm lemmas.

results.title: Truncating a projected matrix
results.informal: Bounds of the type $$\|A - Q\lbrack\!\lbrack Q^\top A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k\|_F^2 \le \|A - \lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k\|_F^2 + 2\|(I-QQ^\top)A\|_F^2,$$ and the exact identity for the early-truncated variant.
results.conclusion: $\|A - Q\lbrack\!\lbrack Q^\top A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k\|_F^2 \le \|A - \lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k\|_F^2 + 2\|(I-QQ^\top)A\|_F^2$, and an exact identity for the early-truncated variant

results.title: Tail of the singular value sequence
results.informal: $\sigma_{\ell+1}^2 \le \frac{1}{\ell-k}\sum_{i>k}\sigma_i^2$; that is, for $t \ge 4k$, $$\sigma_{\lceil t/2\rceil+1}^2 \le \frac{4}{t}\cdot\mathrm{OPT}^2.$$

formalizations.usage: Pass an antitone nonnegative `σ : ℕ → ℝ` (e.g. `singularValues A`), `ht : 0 < t`, `hℓ : ℓ = (t + 1) / 2`, `hk : 4 * k ≤ t` and `hN : ℓ ≤ N`; gives `σ ℓ ^ 2 ≤ 4 / t * ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico k N, σ j ^ 2`.
Pass an antitone nonnegative `σ : ℕ → ℝ` and `hk : k < ℓ`; gives `σ ℓ ^ 2 ≤ (∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico k ℓ, σ j ^ 2) / (ℓ - k)`.

results.title: Power-iteration error amplification
results.informal: For $Y = (AA^\top)^qA\Omega$ and $Q = \operatorname{orth}(Y)$: $$\|(I-QQ^\top)A\| \le \|(I-QQ^\top)(AA^\top)^qA\|^{1/(2q+1)}.$$ Turns the RSVD bound into a bound with $\sigma_{k+1}^{2q+1}$ decay.
results.notes: The deterministic half of subspace iteration; cheap once the SVD API exists.

results.title: Nyström approximation error for PSD matrices
results.informal: For PSD $A$ and any $\Omega$: $A \succeq A\langle\Omega\rangle := A\Omega(\Omega^\top A\Omega)^\dagger\Omega^\top A \succeq 0$, and $A - A\langle\Omega\rangle$ is the Schur complement. Moreover $\|A - A\langle\Omega\rangle\| \le \|(I-P)A^{1/2}\|^2$ for $P$ the projector onto $\operatorname{range}(A^{1/2}\Omega)$. Foundation for Nyström, RPCholesky and Nyström preconditioning.
results.conclusion: $0 \preceq A\langle\Omega\rangle \preceq A$, $A - A\langle\Omega\rangle$ is a Schur complement, and $\|A - A\langle\Omega\rangle\| \le \|(I-P)A^{1/2}\|^2$

results.title: Sketched regression residual identities
results.informal: For $Q$ orthonormal and $\Psi$ a left sketch, the generalized Nyström core satisfies $\hat{X} = Q^\top A + (\Psi^\top Q)^\dagger\Psi^\top A_\perp$, with $\|Q_\perp^\top E\| = \|E\|$ for $E$ in $\operatorname{range}(Q_\perp)$.
hypotheses: $Q \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times q}$ with orthonormal columns and completion $Q_\perp$, $QQ^\top + Q_\perp Q_\perp^\top = I$
$\Psi \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times s}$ with $\Psi^\top Q$ of full column rank
results.conclusion: $\hat{X} = Q^\top A + (\Psi^\top Q)^\dagger\Psi^\top A_\perp$, $\|A - Q\hat{X}\|_F^2 = \|A_\perp\|_F^2 + \|(\Psi^\top Q)^\dagger\Psi^\top Q_\perp Q_\perp^\top A_\perp\|_F^2$, and $\|Q_\perp^\top E\| = \|E\|$ for $E$ in $\operatorname{range}(Q_\perp)$

formalizations.note: ‖A − Â‖_F² = ‖(I−QQᵀ)A‖_F² + ‖G₁†G₂Q⊥ᵀE‖_F² with G₁ = ΨᵀQ, G₂ = ΨᵀQ⊥; plus sketchedCore/sketchedOutput/coreNoise, the core identity X̂ = QᵀA + coreNoise, ‖Q⊥ᵀE‖_F = ‖E‖_F and its spectral-norm version
formalizations.usage: Pass `hQ : HasOrthonormalCols Q`, the completion `hcomp : Q * Qᵀ + Qp * Qpᵀ = 1` and `hG₁ : IsUnit ((Ψᵀ * Q)ᵀ * (Ψᵀ * Q))`; gives `frobSq (A - sketchedOutput Q Ψ A) = frobSq (residual Q A) + frobSq (pinvL (Ψᵀ * Q) * (Ψᵀ * Qp) * (Qpᵀ * residual Q A))`.
Pass `hQ : HasOrthonormalCols Q`, `hcomp : Q * Qᵀ + Qp * Qpᵀ = 1` and `hG₁ : IsUnit ((Ψᵀ * Q)ᵀ * (Ψᵀ * Q))`; gives `sketchedCore Q Ψ A = Qᵀ * A + coreNoise Q Ψ A`.
Pass `hQ : HasOrthonormalCols Q`, `hQp : HasOrthonormalCols Qp` and `hcomp : Q * Qᵀ + Qp * Qpᵀ = 1`; gives `frobSq (Qpᵀ * residual Q A) = frobSq (residual Q A)`.
Pass `hQ : HasOrthonormalCols Q`, `hQp : HasOrthonormalCols Qp` and `hcomp : Q * Qᵀ + Qp * Qpᵀ = 1`; gives `specNorm (Qpᵀ * residual Q A) = specNorm (residual Q A)`.

results.title: Randomized SVD / range finder expected error
results.informal: For a $t$-column Gaussian test matrix with $t \ge k+2$: $$\mathbb{E}\|A - QQ^\top A\|_F^2 \le \Big(1 + \frac{k}{t-k-1}\Big)\|A - \lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k\|_F^2.$$

formalizations.usage: As `rsvd_main_gaussian` plus `hY : ∀ ω, IsBestRankApprox k ((Q ω)ᵀ * A) (Y ω)`; gives the same bound for `frobSq (A - Q ω * Y ω)`.

Pass the block-SVD hypotheses (`hA`, `hU₂`, `hV₁`, `hV₂`, `hV`), `hkt : k + 2 ≤ t`, `hΩ : μ.map (fun ω => Matrix.of.symm (Ω ω)) = gaussianMatrix n t`, and the a.s. basis facts `hQo`, `hQr`; gives `∫ frobSq (A - Q ω * ((Q ω)ᵀ * A)) ∂μ ≤ (1 + k/(t-k-1)) * frobSq S₂` with no Gaussian or integrability hypotheses.
formalizations.note: unconditional for a Gaussian test matrix: hunit, hinv, hZi and hXi all discharged (the error is bounded by an integrable quantity, and a non-integrable integral is 0)

ported from the LRA project; takes the Gaussian moment identity hinv (E‖S₂Ω₂Ω₁†‖_F² = k/(t−k−1)‖S₂‖_F²) and the a.s. structural facts as hypotheses, as the source does. The hypothesis-free Gaussian version follows from gaussian-conditioning + pinv-frob-moment (next step).
formalizations.usage: Pass the block split `hA` with `hU₂ hV₁ hV₂ : HasOrthonormalCols _` and `hV : V₁ᵀ * V₂ = 0`, `hkt : k + 2 ≤ t`, random `Ω`, `Q` with a.e. `HasOrthonormalCols (Q ω)` (`hQo`) and range inclusion (`hQr`), a.e. `hunit`, the moment identity `hinv` (from `rsvd_inverse_moment_factor`, `integral_pinvR_frobSq_block`, `pinv_frobenius_moment`) and integrability `hXi`, `hZi`; gives `∫ frobSq (A - Q ω * ((Q ω)ᵀ * A)) ∂μ ≤ (1 + k / (t - k - 1)) * frobSq S₂`.

Same hypotheses as `rsvd_main` plus `hY : ∀ ω, IsBestRankApprox k ((Q ω)ᵀ * A) (Y ω)` and integrability of `frobSq (A - Q ω * Y ω)`; gives `∫ frobSq (A - Q ω * Y ω) ∂μ ≤ (1 + k / (t - k - 1)) * frobSq S₂`.

Scalar assembly step: pass the pointwise bound `hX : ∀ ω, X ω ≤ OPTsq + Zsq ω`, `hZ : ∫ Zsq = k / (t - k - 1) * OPTsq` and integrability of `X` and `Zsq`; gives `∫ X ∂μ ≤ (1 + k / (t - k - 1)) * OPTsq`.

results.notes: Both the conditional form (Gaussian facts as expectation hypotheses, ported from the LRA project) and the unconditional Gaussian form are proved; only the user's choice of orthonormal basis Q enters as a hypothesis.

results.title: Generalized Nyström expected error
results.informal: $$\mathbb{E}\|A - A\Omega(\Psi^\top A\Omega)^\dagger\Psi^\top A\|_F^2 \le \Big(1 + \frac{q}{s-q-1}\Big)\Big(1 + \frac{k}{t-k-1}\Big)\mathrm{OPT}^2.$$
hypotheses: $\Omega \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times t}$ and $\Psi \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times s}$ independent standard Gaussian

formalizations.usage: Pass fixed `Q`, `Qp`, `A` with `hQ`, `hQp`, `hcomp : Q * Qᵀ + Qp * Qpᵀ = 1`, `1 ≤ q`, `q + 2 ≤ s`, and `hΨ : μ.map (fun ω => Matrix.of.symm (Ψ ω)) = gaussianMatrix m s`; gives `∫ frobSq (A - sketchedOutput Q (Ψ ω) A) = (1 + q/(s-q-1)) * frobSq (residual Q A)` exactly.

Pass the block-SVD hypotheses, sizes `k+2 ≤ t`, `t+2 ≤ s`, `q ≤ t`, `1 ≤ q`, the laws `hΩ`, `hΨ`, independence `hind : IndepFun (Ω as array) (Ψ as array) μ`, and the basis as a measurable function of Ω (`hQ : ∀ ω, Q ω = Qf (Matrix.of.symm (Ω ω))`, `hQf` entrywise measurable) with a.s. `hQo`, `hQr`; gives `∫ frobSq (A - sketchedOutput (Q ω) (Ψ ω) A) ∂μ ≤ (1 + t/(s-t-1)) * ((1 + k/(t-k-1)) * frobSq S₂)`.
formalizations.note: unconditional generalized Nyström bound for independent Gaussian sketches; the conditional step is Fubini via lintegral_of_indepFun with the completion chosen internally

Chen–Persson thm:GN / Tropp–Webber Thm 5.1; the completion lemma and both forms of the theorem, Gaussian facts as expectation hypotheses (hinv, hcond or hG). Row index types Fin m, Fin n (the source allows any Fintype).
formalizations.usage: Pass the `rsvd_main` hypotheses plus `hts : t + 2 ≤ s`, `hqt : q ≤ t`, the sketch `Ψ`, the conditional completion identity `hcond : E frobSq (A - sketchedOutput Q Ψ A) = E[(1 + q / (s - q - 1)) * frobSq (residual Q A)]` and integrability `hYi`, `hZi`; gives `∫ frobSq (A - sketchedOutput (Q ω) (Ψ ω) A) ∂μ ≤ (1 + t / (s - t - 1)) * ((1 + k / (t - k - 1)) * frobSq S₂)`.

Like `gn_main` but `hcond` is replaced by a completion `Qp` with a.e. `hcomp : Q * Qᵀ + Qp * Qpᵀ = 1`, a.e. `hG₁ : IsUnit ((Ψᵀ * Q)ᵀ * (Ψᵀ * Q))`, the noise-moment identity `hG` (from `completion_inverse_moment_factor`) and integrability `hGi`; same conclusion.

For fixed `Q` (`HasOrthonormalCols`, `1 ≤ q`), its completion `Qp` (`hQp`, `hcomp`), `hqs : q + 2 ≤ s`, random `Ψ` with a.e. `hG₁`, the factorisation `hG₂` (from `completion_inverse_moment_factor`), `hG₁m : ∫ frobSq (pinvL (Ψᵀ * Q)) = q / (s - q - 1)` and integrability `hGi`; gives `∫ frobSq (A - sketchedOutput Q (Ψ ω) A) ∂μ = (1 + q / (s - q - 1)) * frobSq (residual Q A)`.

Scalar assembly step: pass `0 ≤ k`, `k + 2 ≤ t`, `t + 2 ≤ s`, `0 ≤ Y`, `hc : cfac ω ≤ 1 + t / (s - t - 1)`, `hcond : ∫ X = ∫ cfac * Y`, `hstruct : Y ω ≤ OPTsq + Zsq ω`, `hZ : ∫ Zsq = k / (t - k - 1) * OPTsq` and integrability of `cfac * Y`, `Y`, `Zsq`; gives `∫ X ∂μ ≤ (1 + t / (s - t - 1)) * ((1 + k / (t - k - 1)) * OPTsq)`.

results.notes: Both the conditional form (Gaussian facts as expectation hypotheses, ported from the LRA project) and the unconditional Gaussian form are proved; only the user's choice of orthonormal basis Q enters as a hypothesis.

results.title: Truncated generalized Nyström expected error
results.informal: Constant-factor expected Frobenius error for the truncated one-pass estimator with $s \ge 4t$ and $t \ge 4k$.
hypotheses: $\Omega \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times t}$ and $\Psi \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times s}$ independent standard Gaussian
results.conclusion: $\mathbb{E}\|A - \hat{A}_k\|_F^2 \le C\cdot\|A - \lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k\|_F^2$ for an absolute constant $C$, where $\hat{A}_k$ is the rank-$k$ truncated generalized Nyström output

formalizations.note: conditional on hcore, hresid, hVN

results.title: Early-truncated RSVD
results.informal: Error of the early-truncated range finder via decoupled moments of $w$ and $\chi$ and tail integrals of $\sigma_{\min}(\Omega_1)$.
hypotheses: $\Omega$ a standard Gaussian test matrix with $\Omega_1 = V_1^\top\Omega$
results.conclusion: the expected Frobenius error of the early-truncated range finder is at most a factor times $\mathrm{OPT}^2 = \|A - \lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k\|_F^2$, the factor built from decoupled moments of $w$ and $\chi$ and tail integrals of $\sigma_{\min}(\Omega_1)$

results.title: Early-truncated generalized Nyström
results.informal: Combines the early-truncated RSVD bound with the Gaussian completion step.
hypotheses: $\Omega \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times t}$ and $\Psi \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times s}$ independent standard Gaussian
results.conclusion: the early-truncated generalized Nyström output has expected Frobenius error at most a constant times $\|A - \lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k\|_F^2$ (the early-truncated RSVD bound composed with the Gaussian completion step)

results.title: Randomized SVD deviation bounds
results.informal: High-probability versions of the RSVD bound with explicit failure probabilities.
results.conclusion: with probability at least $1 - 2t^{-p} - e^{-u^2/2}$, $\|(I-QQ^\top)A\|_F \le \big(1 + t\sqrt{12k/p}\big)\big(\sum_{j>k}\sigma_j^2\big)^{1/2} + ut\,\frac{e\sqrt{k+p}}{p+1}\,\sigma_{k+1}$, and the spectral analogue

results.title: Subspace iteration expected error
results.informal: $$\mathbb{E}\|A - QQ^\top A\| \le \Big[\Big(1 + \sqrt{\tfrac{k}{p-1}}\Big)\sigma_{k+1}^{2q+1} + \frac{e\sqrt{k+p}}{p}\Big(\sum_{j>k}\sigma_j^{2(2q+1)}\Big)^{1/2}\Big]^{1/(2q+1)}.$$

results.title: Randomized Nyström expected error
results.informal: For Gaussian $\Omega$: $$\mathbb{E}\|A - A\langle\Omega\rangle\|_* \le \Big(1 + \frac{k}{t-k-1}\Big)\|A - \lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k\|_*.$$

results.title: Randomly pivoted Cholesky error bound
results.informal: After $k \ge r/\varepsilon + r\log(1/(\varepsilon\eta))$ pivots, a bound of the type $$\mathbb{E}\operatorname{tr}(A - \hat{A}) \le (1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{tr}\big(A - \lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_r\big) + \eta.$$

results.title: Block Krylov low-rank approximation
results.informal: Block Krylov with $q = O(\log(d/\varepsilon)/\sqrt{\varepsilon})$ iterations gives $(1+\varepsilon)\sigma_{k+1}$ spectral error; gap-independent.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, target rank $k$, Gaussian starting block
results.conclusion: with high probability the output $Z$ (orthonormal, rank $k$) satisfies $\|A - ZZ^\top A\| \le (1+\varepsilon)\sigma_{k+1}(A)$

results.title: Hutchinson estimator is unbiased
results.informal: If $\mathbb{E}\,zz^\top = I$ then $\mathbb{E}[z^\top Az] = \operatorname{tr}A$. Holds for Gaussian, Rademacher and any isotropic $z$.

formalizations.note: pairwise independent, mean-zero, unit-variance coordinates on an abstract probability space
formalizations.usage: Pass a random vector `z : Ω → n → ℝ` with `MemLp 2` coordinates (`hz`), pairwise independent coordinates (`hind`), `hmean : E z_i = 0` and `hsq : E z_i² = 1`; gives `∫ quadForm A (z ω) ∂μ = A.trace` for any square `A`.

results.title: Variance of Gaussian and Rademacher trace estimators
results.informal: $\operatorname{Var}[g^\top Ag] = 2\|A\|_F^2$ (Gaussian $g$, symmetric $A$) and $\operatorname{Var}[\varepsilon^\top A\varepsilon] = 2\big(\|A\|_F^2 - \sum_i A_{ii}^2\big)$ (Rademacher $\varepsilon$).
hypotheses: $g$ standard Gaussian, or $\varepsilon$ with i.i.d. Rademacher entries

formalizations.note: general fourth-moment variance identity for any A (no symmetry), symmetric specialisation 2(‖A‖_F² − ΣA_ii²) + (m₄−1)ΣA_ii², and the m₄ = 3 (Gaussian) and m₄ = 1 (Rademacher) corollaries; proof uses iIndepFun.integral_fun_prod_comp rather than Isserlis
formalizations.usage: Pass a.e.-measurable coordinates with `hindep : iIndepFun (fun i ω => z ω i) μ`, `hmean`, `hsq`, integrable fourth powers `h4` and a common fourth moment `hm4 : E z_i⁴ = m₄`; gives `variance (quadForm A ∘ z) μ = ∑ A i j ^ 2 + ∑ A i j * A j i + (m₄ - 3) * ∑ A i i ^ 2` for any (not necessarily symmetric) `A`.
Same coordinate hypotheses as `variance_quadForm` plus `hA : A.IsSymm`; gives `variance (quadForm A ∘ z) μ = 2 * (frobSq A - ∑ A i i ^ 2) + (m₄ - 1) * ∑ A i i ^ 2`.
Pass `hA : A.IsSymm` and the coordinate hypotheses with `hm4 : E z_i⁴ = 3` (Gaussian-like; Gaussianity itself is not needed); gives `variance (quadForm A ∘ z) μ = 2 * frobSq A`.
Pass `hA : A.IsSymm` and the coordinate hypotheses with `hm4 : E z_i⁴ = 1` (Rademacher-like); gives `variance (quadForm A ∘ z) μ = 2 * (frobSq A - ∑ A i i ^ 2)`.

results.notes: Corollaries assume only the fourth moment m₄, not the Gaussian or Rademacher law; connecting them to gaussianMatrix / a Rademacher law is a small follow-up.

results.title: Tail bounds for trace estimators
results.informal: $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ sample complexity $m = O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\delta))$ for PSD $A$; Cortinovis–Kressner bounds for indefinite $A$ via Hanson–Wright.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ symmetric (PSD for the Avron–Toledo bound)
$m$ i.i.d. Gaussian or Rademacher test vectors
results.conclusion: $m = O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\delta))$ samples give $|\operatorname{tr}_m(A) - \operatorname{tr}A| \le \varepsilon\operatorname{tr}A$ with probability at least $1 - \delta$ for PSD $A$; for indefinite $A$ the Cortinovis–Kressner bound holds with $\|A\|_F$ in place of $\operatorname{tr}A$

results.title: Stochastic diagonal estimation
results.informal: $\mathbb{E}[z \odot Az] = \operatorname{diag}(A)$ for isotropic $z$ with independent entries; variance per coordinate.
results.conclusion: $\mathbb{E}[z \odot Az] = \operatorname{diag}(A)$, with an explicit per-coordinate variance

results.title: Hutch++ error bound
results.informal: $O(1/\varepsilon)$ matrix-vector products suffice for $(1\pm\varepsilon)$ relative trace error on PSD $A$.
hypotheses: $m = O(1/\varepsilon)$ matrix–vector products (times $\log(1/\delta)$ for failure probability $\delta$)
results.conclusion: the Hutch++ estimate $\widehat{\operatorname{tr}}$ satisfies $|\widehat{\operatorname{tr}} - \operatorname{tr}A| \le \varepsilon\operatorname{tr}A$ with probability at least $1 - \delta$

results.title: Exchangeability-based estimators are unbiased
results.informal: Leave-one-out low-rank corrections preserve unbiasedness by exchangeability of the test vectors.
results.conclusion: each leave-one-out low-rank-corrected estimate $\hat{t}_i$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}\,\hat{t}_i = \operatorname{tr}A$, hence so does the average $\frac{1}{m}\sum_i \hat{t}_i$

results.title: Spectral measure of a vector and moments uᵀf(A)u
results.informal: For Hermitian $A$ and unit $u$, $\mu_u = \sum_i |\langle u, v_i\rangle|^2\delta_{\lambda_i}$ satisfies $u^\top f(A)u = \int f\,d\mu_u$, and $\mathbb{E}_g[g^\top f(A)g] = \operatorname{tr}f(A)$.
results.conclusion: $\mu_u = \sum_i |\langle u, v_i\rangle|^2\delta_{\lambda_i}$, so that $u^\top f(A)u = \int f\,d\mu_u$ and $\mathbb{E}_g[g^\top f(A)g] = \operatorname{tr}f(A)$

results.title: Krylov subspaces and their polynomial characterization
results.informal: $$\mathcal{K}_q(A, b) = \operatorname{span}\{b, Ab, \dots, A^{q-1}b\} = \{p(A)b : \deg p < q\}.$$ Nesting, invariance, and dimension at most $q$.
results.conclusion: $\mathcal{K}_q(A, b) = \operatorname{span}\{b, Ab, \dots, A^{q-1}b\} = \{p(A)b : \deg p < q\}$, with $\mathcal{K}_q \subseteq \mathcal{K}_{q+1}$, $A\mathcal{K}_q \subseteq \mathcal{K}_{q+1}$ and $\dim\mathcal{K}_q \le q$

formalizations.note: polynomial characterisation, nesting, A-invariance into the next space, dimension bound
formalizations.usage: Pass `hq : 0 < q`; rewrites `x ∈ krylovSpace A b q ↔ ∃ p, p.natDegree < q ∧ x = (aeval A p).mulVec b`.
No hypotheses (valid also for `q = 0`); rewrites `x ∈ krylovSpace A b q ↔ ∃ p, p.degree < q ∧ x = (aeval A p).mulVec b`.
Pass `h : q ≤ q'`; gives `krylovSpace A b q ≤ krylovSpace A b q'`.
From `hx : x ∈ krylovSpace A b q`; gives `A.mulVec x ∈ krylovSpace A b (q + 1)`.
No hypotheses; gives `Module.finrank ℝ (krylovSpace A b q) ≤ q`.

results.title: Lanczos three-term recurrence and tridiagonalization
results.informal: In exact arithmetic the Lanczos vectors are orthonormal, span $\mathcal{K}_q(A,b)$, and satisfy $$AQ_q = Q_qT_q + \beta_q\,q_{q+1}e_q^\top$$ with $T_q$ Jacobi (tridiagonal).
hypotheses: $q$ steps without breakdown, in exact arithmetic
results.conclusion: the Lanczos vectors $Q_q$ are orthonormal and span $\mathcal{K}_q(A,b)$, and $AQ_q = Q_qT_q + \beta_q\,q_{q+1}e_q^\top$ with $T_q$ symmetric tridiagonal (Jacobi)

results.title: Lanczos quadrature is Gauss quadrature on the spectral measure
results.informal: $e_1^\top f(T_q)e_1 = \int f\,d\hat{\mu}$, where $\hat{\mu}$ is the $q$-point Gauss quadrature rule for $\mu_b$; exact for polynomials of degree at most $2q-1$.
hypotheses: $A$ symmetric and $b$ a unit vector with spectral measure $\mu_b$
$T_q$ the Lanczos tridiagonal matrix after $q$ steps
results.conclusion: $e_1^\top f(T_q)e_1 = \int f\,d\hat{\mu}$, where $\hat{\mu}$ is the $q$-point Gauss quadrature rule for $\mu_b$; it equals $b^\top f(A)b$ for polynomials $f$ of degree at most $2q-1$

results.title: Chebyshev polynomial extremal bounds
results.informal: $$\min_{\deg p \le q,\ p(0)=1}\ \max_{[a,b]}|p| = \frac{1}{T_q\big(\frac{b+a}{b-a}\big)},$$ with growth $T_q(1+\gamma) \ge (1+\sqrt{2\gamma})^q/2$ outside $[-1,1]$. Drives CG, Lanczos and block Krylov rates.

results.title: Conjugate gradient κ-bound
results.informal: $$\|x_q - x\|_A \le 2\Big(\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}-1}{\sqrt{\kappa}+1}\Big)^q\|x_0 - x\|_A.$$
hypotheses: $x = A^{-1}b$ and $x_q$ the $q$-th CG iterate from $x_0$

results.title: Random-start power and Lanczos bounds
results.informal: With a Gaussian start, $\mathbb{E}[\lambda_{\max} - \hat{\lambda}_{\max}]/\lambda_{\max} \le C\log(n)/q$ for the power method and $\le C\log^2(n)/q^2$ for Lanczos.
results.conclusion: $\mathbb{E}[\lambda_{\max} - \hat{\lambda}_{\max}]/\lambda_{\max} \le C\log(n)/q$ for the power method and $\le C\log^2(n)/q^2$ for Lanczos

results.title: Stochastic Lanczos quadrature error bound
results.informal: $\operatorname{tr}f(A)$ is estimated to within $\varepsilon$ with $m = O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\delta))$ samples and $q = O(\sqrt{\kappa}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ Lanczos steps for analytic $f$.
hypotheses: $A$ symmetric with condition number $\kappa$ and $f$ analytic near the spectrum
$m = O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\delta))$ random test vectors and $q = O(\sqrt{\kappa}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ Lanczos steps
results.conclusion: the SLQ estimate is within $\varepsilon$ of $\operatorname{tr}f(A)$ with probability at least $1 - \delta$

results.title: Sketch-and-solve least squares
results.informal: If $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $[A\ \ b]$ then $$\|A\tilde{x} - b\| \le \frac{1+\varepsilon}{1-\varepsilon}\min_x\|Ax - b\|.$$ With the AMM property the factor is $1+\varepsilon$ with $k = O(d/\varepsilon)$.
results.conclusion: $\|A\tilde{x} - b\| \le \frac{1+\varepsilon}{1-\varepsilon}\min_x\|Ax - b\|$; with the AMM property the factor is $1+\varepsilon$ with $k = O(d/\varepsilon)$

results.title: Sketch-and-precondition conditioning bound
results.informal: If $SA = QR$ and $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-embedding for $\operatorname{range}(A)$ then $$\kappa(AR^{-1}) \le \sqrt{\frac{1+\varepsilon}{1-\varepsilon}}.$$

results.title: Randomized Kaczmarz converges linearly in expectation
results.informal: Choosing row $i$ with probability $\|a_i\|^2/\|A\|_F^2$: $$\mathbb{E}\|x_k - x^*\|^2 \le \Big(1 - \frac{1}{\kappa_F^2}\Big)^k\|x_0 - x^*\|^2,$$ with $\kappa_F = \|A\|_F\|A^\dagger\|$. A one-page proof with large downstream reuse.

formalizations.note: Also sum_paths_le (explicit product-weighted sum over row sequences), expected_sqErr_step_le, expected_sqErr_step_eq. σ enters as the hypothesis ∀ v, σ²(v⬝v) ≤ (Av)⬝(Av), so any lower bound on σ_min works; no full-rank assumption.
formalizations.usage: Pass a solution `hxs : A.mulVec xs = b` and a constant `σ` with `hσ : ∀ v, σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v` (any lower bound on σ_min; no rank assumption); gives `Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x k ≤ (1 - σ ^ 2 / frobSq A) ^ k * (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)`.

results.notes: Proved in full over arbitrary finite index types with finite weighted sums instead of measure theory. Deviation from Strohmer–Vershynin: σ is any constant with σ²‖v‖² ≤ ‖Av‖², which recovers 1 − κ(A)⁻² under full column rank.

results.title: Sketch-and-project convergence
results.informal: With $W = \mathbb{E}[Z]$ the expected projector, $$\mathbb{E}\|x_k - x^*\|_B^2 \le \big(1 - \lambda_{\min}(W)\big)^k\|x_0 - x^*\|_B^2.$$ Recovers Kaczmarz, coordinate descent and block variants.
hypotheses: a consistent system $Ax^* = b$ and a norm-defining $B \succ 0$
a random sketch inducing the $B$-orthogonal projector $Z$, with $W = \mathbb{E}[Z]$

results.title: Nyström-preconditioned CG
results.informal: The condition number of the Nyström-preconditioned system is $O(1)$ once the rank exceeds the effective dimension.
hypotheses: a randomized Nyström approximation $P$ of rank exceeding the effective dimension $d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mu)$
results.conclusion: $\kappa\big(P^{-1/2}(A + \mu I)P^{-1/2}\big) = O(1)$, so preconditioned CG converges at a rate independent of $\kappa(A + \mu I)$

results.title: Conditioning on an independent Gaussian block (tower property)
results.informal: If $Y$ is standard Gaussian and independent of $X$, then $$\mathbb{E}\|S\,Y\,T(X)\|_F^2 = \|S\|_F^2\cdot\mathbb{E}\|T(X)\|_F^2.$$ Applied to the blocks $V_1^\top\Omega$ and $V_2^\top\Omega$, it turns the second-moment identity and the pseudoinverse moment into the expectation hypotheses of the RSVD and generalized Nyström theorems.
hypotheses: $Y$ a standard Gaussian matrix independent of $X$
$S$ fixed and $T(X)$ a measurable matrix-valued function of $X$

formalizations.note: no integrability hypothesis (proved via lintegral); companions integral_of_indepFun / lintegral_of_indepFun (Fubini for independent variables), rsvd_inverse_moment_factor, completion_inverse_moment_factor, integral_pinvR_frobSq_block
formalizations.usage: Pass `hX : AEMeasurable X μ`, `hY : Measure.map Y μ = gaussianMatrix p m`, `hXY : IndepFun X Y μ` and entrywise-measurable `T` (`hT`); gives `∫ frobSq (S * Matrix.of (Y ω) * T (X ω)) ∂μ = frobSq S * ∫ frobSq (T (X ω)) ∂μ`, with no integrability hypothesis.
Pass AE-measurable `X`, `Y` with `hXY : IndepFun X Y μ` and integrability of `g` against `(map X μ).prod (map Y μ)`; gives `∫ g (X ω) (Y ω) ∂μ = ∫ x, ∫ y, g x y ∂(map Y μ) ∂(map X μ)`.

Pass `hΩ : Measure.map Ω μ = gaussianMatrix n t` (array-valued `Ω`; for a matrix-valued `Ω'` instantiate `Ω := fun ω => Matrix.of.symm (Ω' ω)`) and `V₁`, `V₂` with `V₁ᵀV₁ = 1`, `V₂ᵀV₂ = 1`, `V₁ᵀV₂ = 0`; gives `∫ frobSq (S₂ * (V₂ᵀ Ω) * pinvR (V₁ᵀ Ω)) = frobSq S₂ * ∫ frobSq (pinvR (V₁ᵀ Ω))`, i.e. `hinv` of `rsvd_main` up to the inverse moment.

Pass `hΨ : Measure.map Ψ μ = gaussianMatrix m s` and `Q`, `Qp` with `Qᵀ * Q = 1`, `Qpᵀ * Qp = 1`, `Qᵀ * Qp = 0`; gives `∫ frobSq (pinvL (Ψᵀ Q) * (Ψᵀ Qp) * B) = (∫ frobSq (pinvL (Ψᵀ Q))) * frobSq B` for every fixed `B` (hypothesis `hG₂` of `completion_reduction`).

Pass `hΩ : Measure.map Ω μ = gaussianMatrix n t` and `hV₁ : V₁ᵀ * V₁ = 1`; gives `∫ frobSq (pinvR (V₁ᵀ Ω)) ∂μ = ∫ G, frobSq (pinvR (Matrix.of G)) ∂gaussianMatrix k t`, ready for `pinv_frobenius_moment`.

results.notes: Done. Mathlib gaps noted: no MeasurableSpace instance on Matrix; no lemma pulling IndepFun back along a map with a given law.

results.title: Gaussian integration by parts
results.informal: For $g \sim N(0,I_n)$ and smooth $f$ of moderate growth, $$\mathbb{E}[g_i f(g)] = \mathbb{E}[\partial_i f(g)].$$ One-dimensional and multivariate forms.
hypotheses: $f$ differentiable with $f$, $\nabla f$ of moderate growth
results.notes: Port of Prove2me gaussian_ibp_one_dim, gaussian_integration_by_parts.

results.title: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroup: invariance, commutation, entropy derivative
results.informal: The semigroup $P_t f(x) = \mathbb{E} f(e^{-t}x + \sqrt{1-e^{-2t}}\,g)$ leaves the Gaussian measure invariant, commutes with derivatives up to the factor $e^{-t}$, and the entropy of $P_t f$ is differentiable in $t$ with derivative given by the Dirichlet form.
hypotheses: $f$ bounded below and smooth, one dimension
results.notes: Port of ou_semigroup_invariant, ou_semigroup_commutation, ou_entropy_hasDerivAt.

results.title: Gaussian logarithmic Sobolev inequality
results.informal: For the standard Gaussian measure $\gamma_n$ and smooth $f$: $$\operatorname{Ent}_{\gamma_n}(f^2) \le 2\int |\nabla f|^2\,d\gamma_n.$$ Proved in one dimension via the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroup, then tensorised.
results.notes: Port of gaussian_logsobolev_bounded_below, _one_dim_compact_support, _one_dim, gaussian_logsobolev.

results.title: Tensorisation of entropy
results.informal: For a product measure $\mu = \mu_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes \mu_n$: $$\operatorname{Ent}_\mu(f) \le \sum_i \mathbb{E}_\mu\big[\operatorname{Ent}_{\mu_i}(f)\big],$$ where the inner entropy is in the $i$-th coordinate.
hypotheses: $\mu$ a finite product of probability measures
results.notes: Port of entropy_tensorization.

results.title: Herbst's argument
results.informal: A log-Sobolev inequality with constant $c$ implies $\mathbb{E}e^{\lambda F} \le e^{\lambda\mathbb{E}F + c\lambda^2 L^2/2}$ for $L$-Lipschitz $F$, hence Gaussian tails $\mathbb{P}[F \ge \mathbb{E}F + t] \le e^{-t^2/(2cL^2)}$.
hypotheses: $\mu$ satisfies a log-Sobolev inequality with constant $c$
$F$ $L$-Lipschitz (via the entropy bound for Lipschitz functions)
results.notes: Port of herbst_argument, lipschitz_smooth_approx, gaussian_lipschitz_entropy_bound, gaussian_concentration_vector.

results.title: Slepian's tail comparison
results.informal: If $(X_i)$ and $(Y_i)$ are centred Gaussian vectors with $\mathbb{E}(X_i - X_j)^2 \le \mathbb{E}(Y_i - Y_j)^2$ for all $i, j$, then for all $t$: $$\mathbb{P}\big[\max_i X_i \ge t\big] \le \mathbb{P}\big[\max_i Y_i \ge t\big].$$
results.conclusion: $\mathbb{P}[\max_i X_i \ge t] \le \mathbb{P}[\max_i Y_i \ge t]$ for every $t$
results.notes: Port of slepian_tail_comparison (via the smart-path interpolation).

results.title: Sudakov–Fernique inequality
results.informal: Under the Slepian increment condition, $\mathbb{E}\max_i X_i \le \mathbb{E}\max_i Y_i$.
results.notes: Port of sudakov_fernique.

results.title: Gordon's minimax comparison inequality
results.informal: For doubly indexed centred Gaussian processes $X_{ij}, Y_{ij}$ with $\mathbb{E}(X_{ij}-X_{ik})^2 \le \mathbb{E}(Y_{ij}-Y_{ik})^2$ and $\mathbb{E}(X_{ij}-X_{lk})^2 \ge \mathbb{E}(Y_{ij}-Y_{lk})^2$ for $i \ne l$: $$\mathbb{E}\min_i\max_j X_{ij} \le \mathbb{E}\min_i\max_j Y_{ij}.$$ The engine behind the lower bound $\mathbb{E}\,\sigma_{\min}(G) \ge \sqrt{N} - \sqrt{n}$.
hypotheses: $X, Y$ centred Gaussian processes indexed by $i, j$
increment conditions within rows and across rows
results.notes: Port of gordon_minimax, expectation_norm_gaussian_diff.

results.title: Negative moments of chi-square
results.informal: For $\chi^2_d$ and $q$ with $2q < d$: $\mathbb{E}[(\chi^2_d)^{-q}]$ in closed form via the Gamma function, with the $L^q$ bound $\|(\chi^2_d)^{-1}\|_{L^q} \le C/d$, and $\mathbb{E}[(\chi^2_d)^{-2}] = 1/((d-2)(d-4))$.
results.notes: Port of chi_square_neg_moment, inv_chi_square_Lq_bound, inv_sq_chi_square_moment.

results.title: Expectation from a tail bound (layer cake)
results.informal: If $\mathbb{P}[X > t] \le F(t)$ then $\mathbb{E}X \le a + \int_a^\infty F(t)\,dt$; and $\int_0^\infty t^p e^{-ct}\,dt$ bounds. Turns tail bounds into moment bounds.
results.notes: Port of integral_le_of_tail_bound, integral_power_exp_le.

results.title: Tail of the smallest Wishart eigenvalue
results.informal: For $G \in \mathbb{R}^{r\times k}$ Gaussian, a tail bound $\mathbb{P}[\lambda_{\min}(GG^\top) \le s] \le \ldots$ obtained from the rank-one CDF and a density bound; feeds the pseudoinverse spectral tail.
results.notes: Port of wishart_lambda_min_cdf_rank_one, wishart_lambda_min_cdf_density_bound (the one unproved step on Prove2me: scaffold), wishart_lambda_min_tail, tw_gamma_ratio_bound, tw_inverse_moment_numeric.
